title: Wob's Wiggly Way Adventure
markdown:
Wob the goblin adjusted his spectacles. They were a little too big, which meant they often slid down his nose. He smoothed his tunic, a happy green with a few adventurous brown patches from his explorations. Today was a very, very important day. He wanted to show his elf pen-friend, Faelar, just how clever and organised he was. Faelar lived far away in a sunny meadow. Wob imagined him reading letters in a tidy quiet library that smelled of old paper and dried flowers. Wob’s own room was more like a cozy jumble: interesting pebbles, inventions still being made, colorful drawings.

“Right then,” he announced to his reflection in a shiny pebble on his desk. The pebble winked back. “Operation Moonpetal Moss is a go! First, get the moss. Second, be back by teatime. Third, impress Faelar with all the exact details of my trip.”

He held up a scroll, very detailed, a little smudged with ink. A masterpiece of goblin planning. He knew exactly which path to take. Where the sunbeams would be brightest for the moss to grow. How many steps to the snowy shelves of Candlecrag. He had even figured out the perfect angle for his shovel.

He stepped out of his burrow, a cozy little home tucked into the side of the mountain, and took a deep refreshing breath. Crisp air, pine needles, distant snow. A brisk adventure promised. The mountain woods were usually his absolute favourite place: rustling leaves, chattering squirrels, sunlight dancing through branches, playful shadows on mossy ground. He set off with a determined walk, humming a little tune about excellent organisation and the joy of perfectly done plans.

Soon a flash of pure white zipped past, a blur against the brown forest floor. “Wob! Wob! Going somewhere important?” Pip, the mountain hare, fur as white and fluffy as the snow-dusted rocks. Whiskers twitching with boundless energy. He always seemed to know when an adventure was about to start.

“Indeed, Pip!” Wob puffed his chest and adjusted his spectacles again. “A most important mission to collect moonpetal moss for Faelar. And I have a plan.” He tapped the precious scroll with a happy flourish.

Pip giggled, dry leaves skittering. “Plans are good! But sometimes the best way is the wiggly way!” He pointed with his nose toward a path that was barely there, winding between old fir trees covered in moss. More like a deer’s secret passage than a proper trail. “This way is much faster if you know the whispers of the wind and the secrets of the roots.”

Wob hesitated. Brow furrowed. His scroll did not mention wiggly ways or whispers of the wind. It was all straight lines and measured steps. But Pip was usually right about shortcuts. He had a knack for the mountain’s hidden routes. “Very well, Pip. Lead on!” He rolled the scroll carefully.

Deeper in, the trees grew taller and more grand, branches heavy with thick blankets of fresh snow. A deep hush. Playful shadows became a soft gentle light through snowy tops. High above, on a strong snow-laden branch, a great owl blinked wise amber eyes.

“Hoo-hoo.” Soft sigh of wind through pines. “The path you seek is not always the straightest one, young goblin. Sometimes the moss grows where the unexpected calls, where curiosity leads.”

They called her Luna Bright. Her pronouncements often made Wob scratch his head, but they had a funny way of making sense later, like puzzle pieces fitting together.

A strong gust swirled around them, stronger than before, carrying big feathery snowflakes that danced and tumbled like tiny ballerinas. The world outside Wob’s immediate sight turned a soft hazy white. He could not see Pip.

“Pip?” A little tremor of worry, a tiny mouse in his tummy. A prickle of unease. Unknown territory. Not on the scroll.

He stumbled forward, pushing through a thicket of snow-laden branches that tickled his nose. Then he stopped. Before him, in a small clearing bathed in a strange bluish light that seemed to come from the air itself, was a scene of utter delightful chaos. A wizened wizard, beard like a grumpy storm cloud that crackled with tiny sparks, was trying to get a rather stubborn-looking goat to do something. The goat, whose name Wob later learned was Gerty, had a mischievous clever glint in her eye. Little horns seemed to sparkle.

“Come now, Gerty.” Raspy as dry leaves. “Just one simple charm for the frosty ground. Slippery-Slide-Away-Today!” He waved his gnarled staff with a flourish.

Gerty let out a loud defiant Baaa and kicked her hind legs with surprising force. Instead of making the ground slippery, a torrent of shimmering impossibly icy mist shot from her horns. It coated the clearing and a good part of the surrounding woods in a layer of glistening impossibly smooth ice. Wob gasped, eyes wide behind his spectacles. The moonpetal moss, the very reason for his journey, was just beyond the tricky ice.

“Oh, for the love of a good potion!” The wizard threw his hands up. His grumpy beard practically vibrated. “Every time! Gerty, you have the knack for making things freeze like a bewildered badger!”

Wob looked at the shimmering ice, then at the distant moss, then at his now completely useless scroll. It suddenly felt very silly. The familiar flutter in his tummy, the one that happened when things were not quite as organised and predictable as he liked. He remembered Luna Bright: the moss grows where the unexpected calls. Perhaps this chaotic ice was part of the unexpected call.

Pip reappeared as if by magic, skidding to a halt. “Whoa! That Gerty’s got a knack for making things zippy!” Nose twitching rapidly.

The wizard, Grumbles, spotted them. “Well, well. A small green visitor in my personal ice rink? Come for a spot of amateur ice-skating, have you?”

Wob took a deep breath. Heart a little faster. He was not going to impress Faelar with a perfectly executed plan today. Maybe he could impress him with a tale of a brave moonlit adventure and a wizard with a goat who could make ice. Pip, always ready with a quick hop. Luna Bright, offering wise if puzzling advice from above. And himself, trying his very best even when plans went topsy-turvy.

“Excuse me, Wizard Grumbles.” Voice surprisingly steady, as if he had been planning this moment all along. “We need to get to the snowy shelves to collect some moonpetal moss. Do you suppose Gerty’s spell could perhaps help us cross this icy patch? Maybe make it a little more slippery?”

Grumbles stroked his magnificent grumpy beard. A thoughtful frown. “Help you? That goat once turned my prize-winning mandrake into a squeaky toy. But…” He eyed Gerty, who was already trying to lick the frost off a pinecone with great concentration. “She is remarkably good at making things slide.”

Pip nudged Wob, eyes twinkling. “Maybe if Gerty makes it extra slippery, we can slide right over there like on a toboggan!”

And so, with a hopeful nod from Pip and a resigned sigh from Grumbles, Wob coaxed Gerty into a more enthusiastic blast of icy mist, this time aimed strategically toward the shelves where the moss grew. Then, Pip holding his hand tightly and Grumbles shouting mostly encouragingly, with a few mind-the-branches mixed in, Wob and Pip zoomed across the ice on a makeshift sled of large fallen bark. They landed with a soft snowy thud right beside a patch of the most beautiful silvery moonpetal moss Wob had ever seen. It shimmered like captured moonlight.

Collecting was quick work. Fingers nimble despite the cold. The journey back, sliding most of the way thanks to Gerty’s continuing unexpected bursts of frost, was surprisingly fast and full of laughter. Wob even managed to jot notes for Faelar in a small notebook from his pocket: the spontaneous ice-generating nature of young goats; the unexpected efficiency of a well-timed gravity-assisted slide.

When he finally arrived back at his burrow, the moon was high, casting long peaceful shadows. He had not returned by teatime. His scroll was a relic of a forgotten plan. He carefully placed the shimmering moss beside his writing quill. A warm contented feeling spread through him and chased away the last of the chill. He had not been perfectly organised. He had been brave. He had been resourceful. And he had an amazing unexpected story to tell Faelar.

He smiled, a genuine Wob-sized smile that crinkled the corners of his eyes. The pebble on the desk, when he glanced at it, seemed to wink again. The wiggly way, it turned out, had better ice.
characters: Wob (spectacled goblin with a detailed scroll), Pip (white mountain hare)
